headline: Low prompt-injection and data-sharing risk; no direct write-conflict or compliance breach is evidenced for caveman + pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and multiple API-backed tools, so if pathway feeds its outputs into caveman via a shared channel, prompt injection is possible. pathway has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP surface, so the bridge is not default. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited and requires unusual integration.
conditions: IF caveman is connected to pathway outputs through MCP or another shared channel, injection becomes reachable.
IF pathway content is treated as instructions by caveman, malicious text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP bridge between the agents.
Route pathway output through a sanitizer that strips imperative text.
Require human review before caveman acts on pathway-generated content.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while pathway exposes no filesystem read/write or network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound transfer in the profiles, leakage is not default; any exposure would require an external bridge or operator misconfiguration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, caveman may expose notes or logs to pathway-adjacent workflows.
IF an external orchestrator copies caveman files into pathway inputs, sensitive project notes can leak.
mitigations: Keep separate directories and mounts for each agent.
Do not pass CLAUDE.md, memory files, or session logs into pathway.
Review orchestrator file-copy rules before enabling the pair.
Turn off any automatic export of caveman artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement per-file access controls and audit logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances, but pathway cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Because pathway has no mutable write surface and caveman has no documented shared writable target here, the pairwise write-conflict pathway is effectively blocked.
conditions: IF pathway is given write access outside this profile, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
IF an orchestrator adds a shared mutable directory, concurrent edits could collide.
mitigations: Keep pathway read-only.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Serialize any external writes through one coordinator.
Use per-agent output folders.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can generate project notes and other text that pathway could ingest, so a bad or hallucinated output can cascade if pathway treats it as authoritative. pathway is a document-processing system, which makes this a plausible default workflow even though direct action-taking is not shown. The risk is moderate because verification is absent in the profiles.
conditions: IF pathway ingests caveman-generated documents without validation, errors can propagate downstream.
IF caveman writes speculative content into project notes, pathway may preserve or transform the mistake.
mitigations: Add a verification step before pathway consumes caveman output.
Mark caveman-generated files as untrusted by default.
Require source citations in any handoff document.
Sample-check transformed outputs before publication.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatch is evidenced. caveman lists token usage, session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while pathway lists no data classes touched and no compliance constraints. Without a documented regulated-data flow, a compliance breach is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the pair, compliance must be reassessed.
IF either agent is later deployed under a residency or retention constraint, the current assessment no longer applies.
mitigations: Classify data before use.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings for any shared artifacts.
Review vendor residency requirements.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
